# The problem

## DES is a queue engine you only need when there's a queue

![](/Users/johngraves/Dropbox/Projects/des-resource-constraints/figures/congestion.png){width=70%}

- A cohort of patients, each progressing through Sick-Sicker on their own clock.
- Add **one finite treatment resource** (capacity `c` ≪ demand) and patients must **wait**.
- The disease must keep progressing *while they wait*. That is the whole problem.

## The naive fix breaks face validity {.smaller}

A finite `seize()` **blocks the arrival** — which freezes that patient's hand-rolled
event clock. They can't die, progress, or recover while queued.

![](/Users/johngraves/Dropbox/Projects/des-resource-constraints/figures/petri-token-queue.png){width=55%}

> Restricting treatment *prevented* simulated deaths instead of causing them — the
> **freeze trap** (Model 8). The shared invariant any fix must honor: **the patient must never block.**

# Two faithful designs

## Approach A — endogenous-wait registry event

- A real capacity-`c` resource + a **fire-time free-slot guard** (cap enforced exactly).
- The wait is computed analytically from **live occupancy** — longer when more compete.
- Adds contention **without touching the decade-stable `main_loop.R` engine**.

## Approach B — claim-ticket companion

- A companion trajectory holds a real **FIFO `seize()` queue** + per-patient `send`/`trap` + `renege`.
- The **exact emergent** queue, at the cost of more moving parts.

## A ≈ B on the CEA endpoints

- A and B agree on mean deaths, S2-time, dQALY, dcost **within Monte-Carlo noise**.
- They differ only by construction on the **wait distribution** (B exact FIFO, A analytic).
- Headline: infinite capacity is *dominant*; the constraint forfeits nearly all of that value.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}

set.seed(1)
source(here::here("R/model-A.R"), chdir = TRUE)   # MODEL_A_NORUN=1 to skip its heavy block
# des_run(modifyList(inputs, list(N = 500)))
```
:::


# Takeaways

## Choosing an approach

- **A**: minimal blast radius (a registry event), analytic wait — preferred when you must not
  touch the engine and an analytic wait is acceptable.
- **B**: exact emergent queue — preferred when the wait *distribution* itself is the object of study.
- Both honor the invariant: *patient never blocks; disease progresses during the wait.*

## Where to go deeper

- The full build (Models 1–8 → traps → A → B → validation ladder) is in the **manuscript**:
  `manuscript/resource-contention.qmd`.
- Methods + verified simmer semantics: `design/methodology.md`.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
